messages.subject: Inability to install rstan on Win 7
parts: I followed the instructions on how to install rstan (latest release).  Installed RTools first, got that to work ok.  However, there seems to be a memory issue.  The attached file documents the R session where I tried to install rstan.  Any help as to what is going on?  There is about 95GB of free space on my hard drive, so lack of available storage does not seem to be the problem.  Is there a setting for the R environmental variables that needs to be changed?   Thanks for help.  Larry Gould

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Inability to install rstan on Win 7
parts:
On Wednesday, January 15, 2014 10:41:24 AM UTC-5, Larry Gould wrote:
I followed the instructions on how to install rstan (latest release).  Installed RTools first, got that to work ok.  However, there seems to be a memory issue.  The attached file documents the R session where I tried to install rstan.  Any help as to what is going on?  There is about 95GB of free space on my hard drive, so lack of available storage does not seem to be the problem.  Is there a setting for the R environmental variables that needs to be changed?   Thanks for help.  Larry Gould

Your attachment has lines from the compiler like:
O0 -Wall -mtune=core2 -g -c stanc.cpp -o stanc.o

that come from the Makevars (or other configuration) file(s). You need to find that file and eliminate the -g flag, which generates the debug symbols. The debug symbols are occasionally useful for debugging a model --- which is why there is an rstan function set_cppo('debug') --- but shouldn't be necessary when installing rstan.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Inability to install rstan on Win 7
parts:
This is a messy intersection of Windows, which doesn't have
good C++ tools, and R, which doesn't allow packages to easily
control configuration.

What you need to do is edit a file named "Makevars.win" or
"Makevars", which you will find either here:

R_HOME/.R/Makevars.win

or if that doesn't exist, in

R_HOME/.R/Makevars

where "R_HOME" is the directory into which R is installed.

You need to edit that file and remove the "-g" line from the compiler
configuration.

You also want to make sure it specifies "-O3" (that's a capital "O",
not a zero) and not "-O3". If you can find the Makevars file and
would like more help, just send us the contents of the Makevars file
and we can show you what it should look like. The problem is that
different R packages mess with it, so we can't know what it's going
to look like for users.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Inability to install rstan on Win 7
parts:
On Wednesday, January 15, 2014 2:28:58 PM UTC-5, Larry Gould wrote:
First, thanks for the rapid response.  Unfortunately, you are vastly overestimating my familiarity with issues involving C++ and my ability to deal with them.  Exactly what am I looking for?  Where would I be likely to find it?  What do I do when I find it?  For what it's worth, when I tried to implement STAN some months ago, I could get past this point, but ran into other problems.  Is there something in the installation process that I am missing?    I'd love to be able to use STAN about like I now use OpenBUGS.  Help!

Try this in a fresh R session

Sys.setenv(R_MAKEVARS_USER = "foobar")
options(repos = c(getOption("repos"), rstan = "http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/"))
install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
Sys.unsetenv("R_MAKEVARS_USER")
library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast")

The home directories can get complicated on Windows. I think you can find it by doing

Sys.getenv("HOME")

and looking for a .R directory under there, which should have a Makevars file that will be set optimally for RStan usage but you may need to change it for use with other R packages.

Ben

messages.author: 3d8288d2d8fd30fb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Inability to install rstan on Win 7
parts:
Bob:  

Thank you.  That was the secret of success, although it took forever to find the .R directory (it was not in the directory where the R program and subdirectories were stored).  Not only did the program install, but I also could get the schools example to work which I could not do last time.

You might want in future versions of the startup documentation to make this clear.  What people have to do is (1) find the .R  directory (which could be in their Documents directory and not in the directory where the R code is), (2) remove the '-g' directive from the first line, and (3) change the 'O0' to 'O3'.  Simple addition to the code, but will cause many Windows users of STAN to sing your praise.

Larry

The instructions for installation are getting really clunky because

If someone were willing to break them apart, I think a more natural
arrangement would be a checklist organized by platform.
